why: Rule 1/2: 8023 is the contained, lowest-z end of the only long track (other end exits the z+ face), and the detached 23 cm e-cluster 13 lies collinear with a ray out of 8023, with two sub-cm stubs 11-12 cm away.

Rule 1: the 21 cm proton attached to 15010 runs out to a 203853 e/cm stop at 15007, and its near end is unmeasured rather than cool, so it gives no counter-evidence; rule 2 also puts 15010 7 cm upstream of the rival junction 15017, whose only edge over it is a 9.4 cm stub at x1.36.

Rule 1 on the only real object: the 14.3 cm proton profile declines monotonically from 215000 e/cm at 9000 (matching the proton template anchored there) to 130000 at 9001, so 9000 is the stopping end and 9001 the start.
Rule 1: the single 17 cm proton rises away from 12002 (147847 -> 207743 e/cm at 12000), so 12000 is the Bragg stop and 12002, also the lower-z end, is the origin.
Rule 1 textbook V: 16002 is the apex of a 30 cm MIP track that exits the z+ face and a 2.9 cm 199323 e/cm proton stub, both leaving the same point in the zoom.

Rule 1: cluster 29's 21.7 cm track starts 1.7 cm from 5001 and p4 shows a clean monotone Bragg rise over its last 6 cm to 165000 e/cm at the far end 29007, while the 104 cm muon and two short pi/e stubs leave the same degree-3 point.
Rule 8: the event is a single 0.3 cm blob and 27000 is the only candidate in it, so the pick is forced rather than reasoned.
Rule 1: 11002 is the lowest-z apex of a clean 50 degree V (not the collinear trap) whose 55 cm prong rises away x1.38 and whose other prong is a 21 cm heavily ionising proton.

Rule 1/6: 17019 carries a 5.6 cm proton stub at 226320 e/cm plus a 90 cm pi+ that rises away x1.40, and sits inside a swarm of small EM clusters, whereas the only other structure is a 255 cm straight track with a parallel partner and no junction on it.

Rule 1: 21002 is a 108 degree V where the 49 cm proton rises away x2.32 and p4 shows a monotone rise over its last 10 cm to 220000 e/cm on the proton template at 21001, while the 58 cm muon leaves the other way and exits the z+ face.

Rule 1 in its strongest form: 2 of 2 prongs rise away from 10002 at a 99 degree opening, and p4 confirms both far ends stop - the 228 cm muon decays from 185000 e/cm at 10000 and the 78.5 cm proton rises onto the template to 295000 at 10004.

Topology: 14002 is the apex of a 109 degree V between a MIP 58 cm muon that exits the z+ face and a 22 cm 2x-MIP proton-like prong, but the sheet scores both prongs flat and p4 shows the 14001 end is a hot patch, not a monotone Bragg rise, so rule 1 does not confirm it.
Rule 8: the whole event is one 0.9 cm blip with two candidates 0.9 cm apart and no readable direction, so this is a coin flip between indistinguishable points.

Rule 1: 11003 is a degree-4 hadronic star with two short protons (99401 and 185390 e/cm) and a 33.5 cm pi+ rising away x1.70 whose far end 11000 shows a proper monotone Bragg decay from 290000 e/cm on the proton template in p4.
Rule 1: the 208 cm muon rises away from 13003 x1.39 and a 3.4 cm 191283 e/cm proton stub hangs off the same point, which is also the low-z end of the track.
